reason: The code gap is real, but the value is far below the +0.002 bar. What I checked: in experiments/ext_x138/biohub-x138.ipynb cell 4, 'lowdet peaks' calls _detect_cells_pooled(...,0.3) and never calls _v1284_refine, and 'lowdet write' casts the peaks to int16. In cell 5, readmit (L1249-1297) and the gap filler (L1446) write peaks['vox']. Settings: READMIT 4 um, score >= 0.965; GAPFILL score >= 0.5, cap 3%; EXCLUDE 2 um. The ceiling, recomputed: (a) Share of nodes. Readmitted nodes are 1,337 of 121,777 = 1.10% (CONTEXT.md L1515). No gap-fill count exists anywhere in the repo (exp56/57 notebooks have no outputs), so its 1-2% share is a guess. Total about 2-4% of nodes. (b) What the head does per node. In experiments/coordhead_retrain/out_full_P.log (leak5_f0) the public head moves the mean GT distance from 1.731 to 1.604 um, but the share within 1 um DROPS (0.244 -> 0.225). Matches within 4 um go 22,213 -> 22,205 and within 7 um 23,414 -> 23,413, so it changes 7 um matching by nothing. The head scores only through downstream linking choices (flow relink, readmit anchors, gap gates), which a 0.13-0.74 um move changes only at near-ties. (c) Head total on x138 is +0.007 public. The head drops final nodes by 2.4%, so up to ~0.002 of that may be the node multiplier, leaving ~0.005 from positions. (d) Share x leverage: 0.02-0.04 x 0.005-0.007 x 1-3 = +0.0001 to +0.0009, central about +0.0002-0.0003. The idea's own upper bound (<= +0.001) already sits below the bar. The '3x for removing the coarse grid' factor counts twice: the main peaks were on the same 1.625 um grid before refinement, so the head's measured -7..-9.5% already includes removing the grid. Gains on unseen embryos: the change does not trust network confidence (good), but gap-fill peaks (score 0.5-0.965) are out of distribution for a head trained on >= 0.965 detection-GT pairs from 20 movies. Its shift there has an unknown sign on new embryos, and the head itself adds a y/x bias of +0.35 um. Only the readmit part (1.1%) is in distribution, so the gain that transfers is closer to +0.0001-0.0002. Node count moves by about 0.05% of nodes (+-5% of readmit), which is negligible. LB noise is 0.003 (two identical notebooks scored 0.946 and 0.942), so the change cannot be measured on public, and without a lab it cannot be judged before 29 Sep either. The cited '71% of unmatched annotations have a raw peak within 7 um' is about nodes that are MISSING. Moving coordinates adds no nodes, so that evidence does not support this idea.
fix_if_any: There is no fix that brings it to +0.002 under this lens. The best use is a zero-slot rider with no expected value, after a cheap safety check: (1) refine only the peaks with score >= 0.965 (the readmit set, the same features the head was trained on). A max-pool local maximum does not depend on the threshold (assumed, not checked), so these peaks are exactly the arr peaks the ILP dropped, and their refined coordinates can be reused from arr instead of running the head on low-score gap-fill peaks. Keep gap-fill peaks at their integer positions to avoid applying the head outside its training range. (2) Check it is a byte-identical no-op when off, and on a dummy run that the readmit count stays within +-5%. (3) Ship it only inside an already-planned x138-based finals candidate, never as its own probe. The observation that might matter is a different one: 71% of unmatched annotations have a raw peak within 7 um but no final node (node presence, e.g. a readmit radius/score or gap-fill budget on the refined pool). That is a separate idea and needs its own lab test.
realistic_public_gain: +0.0002 (range -0.0005 to +0.0009); unmeasurable at LB noise 0.003; P(visible on public) < 0.05
realistic_private_gain: +0.0002 (range -0.0005 to +0.0008); only the readmit part (1.1% of nodes, in distribution) transfers with confidence; the gap-fill part is out of distribution for the head
